headline: Hopkinton man critically hurt, dog injured in Sunday SUV crash
dek: A 79-year-old man was hospitalized in critical condition after an SUV struck him near Wood and Fruit streets; police say the driver stayed at the scene and no charges had been filed.
body: A 79-year-old Hopkinton man was critically injured Sunday evening when an SUV struck him while he was walking his dog near the intersection of Wood and Fruit streets, according to police information reported by [CBS Boston](https://www.cbsnews.com/boston/news/hopkinton-pedestrian-hit-walking-dog-wood-street/) and the [Shrewsbury Post](https://shrewsburypost.com/2026/10/11/serious-crash-involving-pedestrian-closes-street-in-hopkinton/). The crash happened at about 6 p.m. Sunday, Oct. 11, as rain was moving through the area.

Police said the man was taken to a hospital and remained in critical condition. His name has not been released. The dog was also struck, and a neighbor brought the animal to the Tufts University Cummings School of Veterinary Medicine for treatment, the reports said. Interim Hopkinton Police Chief Scott van Raalten asked residents to keep the victim and his family in their thoughts, according to a statement quoted by CBS Boston.

The driver was identified by police as a 29-year-old woman from Northborough who was operating a 2018 Nissan Rogue. She remained at the scene and was cooperating with investigators. As of the reports published Sunday night and Monday morning, authorities had filed no charges. Police had not released the names of either the pedestrian or the driver.

The crash brought a heavy police presence to Wood Street, with the section between Fruit and Winter streets expected to remain closed for several hours while an accident-reconstruction team worked at the scene. Drivers were asked to stay away while evidence was documented and investigators worked to establish what happened.

The early public account establishes where and when the collision occurred, the severity of the pedestrian's injuries and the immediate response. It does not establish what caused the collision or whether weather or another factor contributed. Those questions remain for investigators; neither police nor the news reports had announced a final cause, a citation or a criminal charge.

Weather was part of the scene's operating conditions. CBS Boston reported heavy rain Sunday evening as the remnants of Hurricane Isaias moved through Massachusetts, but the report did not say that weather caused the crash. That distinction matters while investigators reconstruct the collision and review any available physical evidence, witness accounts, dash-camera recordings or doorbell-camera footage.

Hopkinton police are asking anyone who saw the crash or has relevant dash-camera or doorbell footage to contact the department. The request could help investigators establish the vehicles' movements and the conditions immediately before impact. Until the investigation produces more information, the known facts are limited to the reported injuries, the damaged dog, the driver's cooperation and the absence of charges as of the latest reports.

For residents, the immediate concern is the man's condition and the dog's recovery. The next public developments are likely to come from the police investigation, any roadway reopening information and a decision about whether charges or citations will be issued. NorthEast News will treat those as separate developments rather than assuming fault from the collision alone.
location: Wood and Fruit streets, Hopkinton, Massachusetts
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Hopkinton man critically hurt in SUV crash while walking dog
seoDescription: A 79-year-old Hopkinton man was critically injured and his dog was struck in a Sunday SUV crash near Wood and Fruit streets, police said.
